QASHANI:87:16-18/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:87:16-18/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:87:16-18/r1.claim: People prefer sensory life and its ornaments, thereby neglecting remembrance of the divine name and prayer because they lack purification; the true spiritual life is better and more enduring.
QASHANI:87:16-18/r1.anchor: تغفلون وتحتجبون عن ذكر ذلك الاسم وصلاة الرب بالحياة الحسية وطيباتها وزخارفها لعدم التزكية

SULAMI:v2p390#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p390#4/r1.speaker: أبو العباس الدينوري
SULAMI:v2p390#4/r1.claim: Low character and ambition choose the world's lowliness; elevated ambition chooses the afterlife, while noble states and sound realities prefer their Lord over both worlds and all they contain.
SULAMI:v2p390#4/r1.anchor: قال أبو العباس الدينوري : من خسأ طبعه وحقرت همته آثر الدنيا بخستها

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419/r1.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419/r1.claim: Ikrima says this addresses the community: you will prefer worldly life.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا قال : يعني هذه الامة ، وانكم ستؤثرون الحياة الدنيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p288/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p288/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p288/r4.claim: Most readers use second-person tuʾthirūn, addressing the polytheists with an abrupt shift; Abu Amr alone reads third-person, referring to the wretched who enter the Fire.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p288/r4.anchor: قرأ الجمهور { تؤثرون } بمثناة فوقية بصيغة الخطاب ، والخطاب موجه للمشركين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p288/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p288/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p288/r5.claim: Bal generally redirects discourse; with coordinated single words it cancels the preceding item, while with clauses it may cancel the claim or simply move to another report, as context determines.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p288/r5.anchor: وحرف { بل } معناه الجامع هو الإضراب ، أي انصراف القول أو الحكم إلى ما يأتي بعد { بل } ؛

TUSTARI:87:16/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:87:16/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:87:16/r1.claim: A believer should regard worldly life like a man on a log at sea, repeatedly calling on God to save him.
TUSTARI:87:16/r1.anchor: ما ينبغي للمؤمن أن يكون في الدنيا إلا كمثل رجل ركب خشبة في البحر

TUSTARI:87:16/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:87:16/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:87:16/r2.claim: God appoints a wise angel to plant kinds of wisdom in the heart of a believer who renounces the world, as worldly people plant orchards.
TUSTARI:87:16/r2.anchor: وما من عبد مؤمن زهد في الدنيا إلا وكل الله به ملكا حكيما يغرس في قلبه أنواع الحكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r10.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r10.claim: Abu Amr alone reads the verb in the third person, referring to the most wretched; Ibn Masud and several early readers share this reading.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r10.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وحده «يؤثرون» بالياء، وقال: يعني الأشقين، وهي قراءة ابن مسعود والحسن وأبي رجاء والجحدري،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r11.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r11.claim: Most readers address the audience directly with the second-person reading; Ubayy's codex expands it as “rather, you prefer.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r11.anchor: وقرأ الباقون والناس: «تؤثرون» بالتاء على المخاطبة، وفي حرف أبي بن كعب «بل أنتم تؤثرون»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r12.claim: People choose the immediate life because they love what is near and are ignorant of the afterlife's lasting character.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r12.anchor: وسبب الإيثار حب العاجل والجهل ببقاء الآخرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن قتيبة وزيد عن يعقوب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92/r1.claim: Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Qutayba, and Zayd from Yaʿqūb read the verb in the third person; the others read it as direct address.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وابن قتيبة وزيد عن يعقوب بل يؤثرون بالياء والباقون بالتاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92/r2.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj prefer direct address because Ubayy ibn Kaʿb transmitted “rather, you prefer” (bal antum tuʾthirūn).
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92/r2.anchor: واختار الفراء والزجاج التاء لأنها رويت عن أبي بن كعب بل أنتم تؤثرون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92/r3.claim: If the address concerns disbelievers, they choose worldly life over the afterlife because they do not believe in it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92/r3.anchor: فإن أريد بذلك الكفار فالمعنى أنهم يؤثرون الدنيا على الآخرة لأنهم لا يؤمنون بها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92/r4.claim: If it concerns Muslims, it means preferring abundant worldly gain to the reward they are promised.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92/r4.anchor: وإن أريد به المسلمون فالمعنى يؤثرون الاستكثار من الدنيا على الإستحسان من الثواب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says the present world came quickly, while the afterlife was described but kept from us, so they chose what was immediate and left what was delayed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p92/r5.anchor: قال ابن مسعود إن الدنيا عجلت لنا وإن الآخرة نعتت لنا وزويت عنا فأخذنا بالعاجل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p382/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p382/r1.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p382/r1.claim: The Prophet calls the world a home for one without a home and wealth for one without wealth, gathered by the senseless.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p382/r1.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "الدنيا دار من لا دار له، ومال من لا مال له، ولها يجمع من لا عقل له

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p382/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p382/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p382/r2.claim: When Ibn Masʿud reached this verse, he stopped and told his companions that they had preferred the world because they saw its adornments, women, food, and drink while the next life was kept from them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p382/r2.anchor: عن عرفجة الثقفي قال: استقرأت ابن مسعود: {سبح اسم ربك الأعلى} فلما بلغ: {بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا} ترك القراءة، وأقبل على أصحابه وقال: آثرنا الدنيا على الآخرة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p382/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p382/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p382/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿud's self-inclusion may be humility and self-abasement, or he may be describing humankind generally; God knows best.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p382/r3.anchor: وهذا منه على وجه التواضع والهضم، أو هو إخبار عن الجنس من حيث (3) هو، والله أعلم.

JISHUMI:v10p7380/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r1.claim: Addressing unbelievers after commands to obey, the author explains that they choose and work for worldly life rather than reflect on the Hereafter.
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r1.anchor: بل تؤثرون تختارون الحياة الدنيا فتعملون لها، وتعمرونها

JISHUMI:v10p7380/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r15.claim: The direct address “you prefer” shows that choosing worldly life is an act of its human subjects.
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r15.anchor: ويدل قوله: (بل تؤثرون) أن اختيارهم ذلك فعلهم

KASHSHAF:87:16/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:16/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:16/r1.claim: People prefer worldly life and therefore fail to do what would make them prosper.

KASHSHAF:87:16/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:16/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:16/r2.claim: A third-person reading is also transmitted; Ibn Masʿud's reading, You prefer, supports the direct-address reading.
KASHSHAF:87:16/r2.anchor: ويعضد الأولى قراءة ابن مسعود : بل أنتم تؤثرون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742/r7.claim: Choosing worldly life means failing to do what brings success; a variant uses third-person plural and Ibn Masud reads an explicit you plural.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r15.claim: One view addresses unbelievers: they prefer worldly life to the afterlife.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r15.anchor: أن المراد بها الكفار , فيكون تأويلها : بل تؤثرون

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r16.claim: Another view addresses Muslims: they prefer accumulating worldly goods to accumulating reward.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p255/r16.anchor: أن المراد بها المسلمون , فيكون تأويلها : يؤثرون الاستكثار

MUQATIL:87:14-19/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:87:14-19/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:87:14-19/r2.claim: People choose the life of this world over the Hereafter.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#5/r1.claim: The addressees prefer worldly life over the hereafter and therefore fail to do what brings success; the addressees are unbelievers.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#5/r1.anchor: على الآخرة فلا تفعلون ما به تفلحون والمخاطب به الكافرون

NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#5/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#5/r2.claim: Abu Amr reads the verb in the third-person plural, “they prefer,” supporting the identification of the addressees as unbelievers.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#5/r2.anchor: دليله قراءة أبى عمرو يؤثرون بالياء

QURTUBI-FULL:87:16/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:16/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو ونصر بن عاصم
QURTUBI-FULL:87:16/r1.claim: They read the verb in the third person, supplying ‘the most wretched’ as its subject; the common second-person reading is supported by Ubayy's ‘rather, you prefer.’
QURTUBI-FULL:87:16/r1.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو ونصر بن عاصم «بل يؤثرون» بالياء على الغيبة

QURTUBI-FULL:87:16/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:16/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:16/r2.claim: On the common second-person reading, the address says that people prefer worldly abundance over abundance of reward.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:16/r2.anchor: وعلى الأول فيكون تأويلها بل تؤثرون أيها المسلمون الاستكثار من الدنيا، للاستكثار من الثواب

QURTUBI-FULL:87:16/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:16/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:87:16/r3.claim: He explains that people chose the present world because its pleasures and food arrived quickly, while the afterlife was unseen, so they took the near and left the deferred.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:16/r3.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود أنه قرأ هذه الآية، فقال: أتدرون لم آثرنا الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة؟

QURTUBI-FULL:87:16/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:16/r4.speaker: أبو موسى
QURTUBI-FULL:87:16/r4.claim: He urges Anas to spend time remembering God after people nearly tear one another apart with talk of worldly matters.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:16/r4.anchor: وروى ثابت عن أنس قال: كنا مع أبي موسى في مسير، والناس يتكلمون

QURTUBI-FULL:87:16/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:16/r5.speaker: أبو موسى
QURTUBI-FULL:87:16/r5.claim: He says the world was hastened and the afterlife hidden; if people saw it, they would never turn away or prefer anything to it.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:16/r5.anchor: ثم قال: يا أنس، ما ثبر الناس! ما بطأ بهم؟ قلت: الدنيا والشيطان والشهوات. قال: لا، ولكن عجلت الدنيا، وغيبت الآخرة

NAHHAS:v5p207/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p207/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p207/r9.claim: The lām may assimilate into the following tāʾ.
NAHHAS:v5p207/r9.anchor: وإن شئت أدغمت اللام في التاء

NAHHAS:v5p207/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p207/r10.speaker: أبي
NAHHAS:v5p207/r10.claim: Ubayy's interpretive reading has antum instead of the verb's second-person plural suffix.
NAHHAS:v5p207/r10.anchor: وفي قراءة أبي ( بل أنتم تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا ) وهذه قراءة على التفسير

NAHHAS:v5p207/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p207/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p207/r11.claim: The reading attributed to Ubayy is an explanatory reading.

NAHHAS:v5p207/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p207/r12.speaker: أبو عمرو
NAHHAS:v5p207/r12.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads yuʾthirūn with yāʾ, referring back to al-ashqā.
NAHHAS:v5p207/r12.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو ( بل يؤثرون ) بالياء على أنه مردود على الأشقى

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.claim: Al-Aʿla is Meccan and has nineteen verses; the Prophet loved it, recited it at Eid and Friday prayers with al-Ghashiya, sometimes on the same day.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.anchor: سورة الأعلى مكية وآياتها تسع عشرة

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.claim: The surah turns the entire cosmos into a sanctuary reverberating with praise and offers the Prophet good news of divine preservation and ease in his mission and affairs.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.anchor: وحق لرسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] أن يحب هذه السورة وهي تحيل له الكون كله معبدا

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.claim: Its foundations are God's oneness as creator, divine revelation, and afterlife recompense, rooted in earlier scriptures; it also portrays the easy nature of the message, messenger, and community.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.anchor: وهي تتضمن الثابت من قواعد التصور الإيماني

QUTB-ZILAL:87:16/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:16/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:16/r1.claim: Preferring worldly life is the root of affliction and neglect: remembrance calls people to account for and prefer the afterlife, while they want and choose this world.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:16/r1.anchor: إن إيثار الحياة الدنيا هو أساس كل بلوى

QUTB-ZILAL:87:16/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:16/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:16/r2.claim: Al-dunya is so named because it is both nearer and lower, base and transient.

RAZI-FULL:v31p135/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p135/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p135/r1.claim: The majority reading uses second-person plural, reinforced by Ubayy’s wording: you prefer worldly work to afterlife work.
RAZI-FULL:v31p135/r1.anchor: قراءة العامة بالتاء ويؤكده حرف أبي ، أي بل أنتم تؤثرون عمل الدنيا على عمل الآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v31p135/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p135/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v31p135/r2.claim: Ibn Masud explains that worldly food, drink, women, and pleasures are immediate and visible, while the afterlife is unseen, so people choose the near reward.
RAZI-FULL:v31p135/r2.anchor: إن الدنيا أحضرت ، وعجل لنا طعامها وشرابها ونساؤها ولذاتها وبهجتها

RAZI-FULL:v31p135/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p135/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو
RAZI-FULL:v31p135/r3.claim: Abu Amr reads in the third person, referring to the most wretched as those who prefer worldly life.
RAZI-FULL:v31p135/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو : يؤثرون بالياء يعني الأشقى

SAMIN-DURR:87:16/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:16/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:87:16/r1.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads the verb in third person; the others use second-person address, and both readings are clear.
SAMIN-DURR:87:16/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو بالغيبة، والباقون بالخطاب، وهما واضحتان.

STUDYQURAN:87:16/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:16/r1.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:87:16/r1.claim: Some take the address about preferring worldly life to be directed at disbelievers.
STUDYQURAN:87:16/r1.anchor: According to some, you is here an address to the disbelievers

STUDYQURAN:87:16/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:16/r2.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:87:16/r2.claim: Others take the address to include all humanity.
STUDYQURAN:87:16/r2.anchor: while others say that it refers to all of humanity

STUDYQURAN:87:16/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:16/r3.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:87:16/r3.claim: A hadith compares the world to a prison for the believer and a garden for the disbeliever.
STUDYQURAN:87:16/r3.anchor: a ḥadīth states, “The world is the prison of the believer and the garden of the disbeliever”

TAB:87:19/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:19/r6.speaker: author
TAB:87:19/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers that the demonstrative covers the nearby verses about purification, prayer, preferring this life, and the better, lasting afterlife, since this is the nearest referent; ṣuḥuf means the books of Abraham and Moses.
TAB:87:19/r6.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب ،   قول من قال :  إن قوله :  قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكى وَذَكَرَ اسمَ رَبّهِ فَصَلّى

TAB-FULL:v24p322#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p322#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p322#2/r1.claim: Qatāda says people choose the immediate world except those God protects.
TAB-FULL:v24p322#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، " {بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا} [الأعلى: 16] فاختار الناس العاجلة إلا من عصم الله.

TAB-FULL:v24p322#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p322#2/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v24p322#2/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd confessed that people choose the visible delights of this world because the afterlife is hidden from them.
TAB-FULL:v24p322#2/r2.anchor: عن عطاء، عن عرفجة الثقفي، قال: استقرأت ابن مسعود سبح اسم ربك الأعلى فلما بلغ: {بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا} [الأعلى: 16] ترك القراءة

TAB-FULL:v24p322#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p322#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p322#2/r3.claim: Most readers use second-person plural taʾthirūn; Abū ʿAmr reads third-person yuʾthirūn of the wretched, but Ṭabarī prefers the majority reading, supported by Ubayy’s wording.
TAB-FULL:v24p322#2/r3.anchor: والذي لا أوثر عليه في قراءة ذلك التاء، لإجماع الحجة من القراء عليه.

TAB-FULL:v24p323/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p323/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p323/r6.claim: Ṭabarī prefers that “this” refers to the nearest preceding lines, 87:14–17, because a demonstrative most naturally points to what is nearby; ṣuḥuf means books or scrolls.
TAB-FULL:v24p323/r6.anchor: وإنما قلت: ذلك أولى بالصحة من غيره، لأن هذا إشارة إلى حاضر، فلأن يكون إشارة إلى ما قرب منها

TABATABAI:87:14-16/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r14.claim: The rebuke addresses human beings generally and their natural attachment to worldly life and its cultivation; the shift to direct address intensifies the reproach.
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r14.anchor: إضراب بالخطاب لعامة الناس على ما يدعو إليه طبعهم البشري من التعلق التام بالدنيا

TABATABAI:87:14-16/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r15.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r15.claim: An alternative view limits the address to unbelievers; either way, the passage is a reproach.
TABATABAI:87:14-16/r15.anchor: وقيل الخطاب للكفار، والكلام على أي حال مسوق للعتاب والالتفات لتأكيده

ZAJJAJ:v5p316/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p316/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p316/r2.claim: The preferred reading has second-person taʾ, supported by Ubayy's explanatory reading بل أنتم تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا; another reading has third-person yāʾ.
ZAJJAJ:v5p316/r2.anchor: والأجود التاء، لأنها رويت عن أبي بن كعب:

TABRISI:87:7-9/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7-9/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو، روح، زيد، قتيبة
TABRISI:87:7-9/r2.claim: These readers use the third-person reading of yuʾthirūn; the other readers address the audience directly.
TABRISI:87:7-9/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وروح وزيد وقتيبة يؤثرون بالياء والباقون بالتاء

TABRISI:87:7-9/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7-9/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:7-9/r4.claim: With the tāʾ reading, the verse directly addresses its listeners; with yāʾ, it refers to the most wretched people.
TABRISI:87:7-9/r4.anchor: وتؤثرون بالتاء على الخطاب بل أنتم تؤثرون والياء على أنه يريد الأشقين

TABRISI:87:10-17/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:10-17/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:10-17/r17.claim: People choose the worldly life, working and building for it while failing to consider the Hereafter.
TABRISI:87:10-17/r17.anchor: أي تختارون { الحياة الدنيا } على الآخرة فتعملون لها وتعمرونها

TABRISI:87:10-17/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:10-17/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:10-17/r18.claim: The rebuke may generally address both believers and unbelievers, since it describes the usual human preference.
TABRISI:87:10-17/r18.anchor: هو عام في المؤمن والكافر بناء على الأعم الأغلب في أمر الناس

THALABI:v10p185/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p185/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p185/r4.claim: The common second-person reading (‘you prefer’) is supported by Ubayy; Abū ʿAmr reads in the third person, referring to the wretched.
THALABI:v10p185/r4.anchor: قراءة العامة: بالتاء وتصديقهم قراءة أبي بن كعب، بل وأنتم تؤثرون

THALABI:v10p185/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p185/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
THALABI:v10p185/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd explains preference for this life by its immediate food, drink, women, and pleasures, while the afterlife is hidden and delayed.
THALABI:v10p185/r5.anchor: قال عرفجة الأشجعي: كنا عند ابن مسعود، فقرأ هذه الآية، فقال لنا: أتدرون لم آثرنا الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p448/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p448/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p448/r4.claim: The common reading addresses the audience directly in the second person, supported by Ubayy’s wording “rather, you prefer.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p448/r4.anchor: (قراءة العامة ب"التاء" (¬4) لما روي في حرف أبي: "بل أنتم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p448/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p448/r5.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p448/r5.claim: People prefer worldly deeds over deeds for the afterlife.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p448/r5.anchor: قال الكلبي: تؤثرون عمل الدنيا على عمل الآخرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p448/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p448/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p448/r6.claim: People choose immediate worldly pleasures because they are present and hastened, while the afterlife is described but withheld from view.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p448/r6.anchor: دار الدنيا أحضرت، وعجل لنا طعامها وشرابها، ونساؤها، ولذتها،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p448/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p448/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p448/r7.claim: Abu Amr reads the verb in the third person, referring to the wicked people described as avoiding the reminder.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p448/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو: {يؤثرون} ب"الياء"، وقال: يعني: الأشقين (¬8) # الذين ذكروا

WAHIDI-QT:87:16/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:87:16/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:87:16/r1.claim: The addressees choose the life of this world.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r12.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r12.claim: People choose and prefer the life of this world.

ELMALILI:87:16-17/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:16-17/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:16-17/r1.claim: Instead of striving for purification and success, heedless people prefer worldly adornment, amusement, food, drink, women, pleasures, and spending wealth on them.
ELMALILI:87:16-17/r1.anchor: dünyâ hayâtı tercih ediyorsunuz onun ziynetini, eğlencesini, yemesini, içmesini, kadınlarını, lezzetlerini takdim ediyor

ELMALILI:87:16-17/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:16-17/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:16-17/r2.claim: At festivals they enjoy passing worldly pleasures more than purifying themselves, giving charity, remembering God, praying, and doing lasting good.
ELMALILI:87:16-17/r2.anchor: Bayram yapmak istediğiniz vakit de temizlik, tasadduk, zikir, namaz, hayr u hasenât gibi sonu felah olan amellerden ziyade gelip geçici dünya lezzetlerinden zevk alıyorsunuz.

ELMALILI:87:16-17/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:16-17/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:16-17/r3.claim: One kind of worldly preference belongs to disbelievers who desire no meeting with God and settle contentedly for this life; cited verses describe their abode and lack of afterlife share.
ELMALILI:87:16-17/r3.anchor: likāullâhı arzu etmeyip sade dünyâ hayâta râzı ve mutmain olan ve ibadet etseler bile yalnız رَبَّنَٓا اٰتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا diyenlerin hâlidir

ELMALILI:87:16-17/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:16-17/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:16-17/r4.claim: A second kind consists of heedless or sinful believers who ask for good in both lives but sacrifice the afterlife when the two interests conflict; their share depends on their deeds.
ELMALILI:87:16-17/r4.anchor: demekle beraber te‘âruz hâlinde dünyayı âhirete tercih edenler, dünya zevki için âhıreti feda eyleyen gāfil veya âsî mü’minlerdir.

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-17:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-17:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-17:anmerkung/r1.claim: For the vocabulary contrasting the present world and the hereafter, the note refers to Q 93:4.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-17:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Zu den für die Gegenüberstellung von Diesseits und Jenseits verwendeten Begrifflichkeiten vgl. die Anmerkung zu 93:4

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r3.claim: Second-person rebukes and the parallel growth of Quranic text and community make it unlikely that early proclamations presuppose a formed community or only follower-only devotional meetings.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r3.anchor: sprechen dagegen, als Sitz im Leben der frühen Verkündigungen lediglich auf Anhänger Muḥammads beschränkte Gemeindeandachten o. Ä. anzunehmen

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-19:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-19:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-19:kommentar/r1.claim: The sura shifts from God addressing the messenger to an abrupt, effective rebuke of hearers for worldly preference and rejection of the message’s core.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-19:kommentar/r1.anchor: Bis hier ist die Sure als Anrede Gottes an den Verkünder gehalten; sie wendet sich erst in einem

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-19:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-19:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-19:kommentar/r2.claim: The earlier typological contrast between good and bad now confronts hearers with a choice and its eschatological consequences.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-19:kommentar/r2.anchor: eingeführte Entgegensetzung von Guten und Bösen, von Seligen und Verdammten wird so in unmittelbaren Bezug zu den Hörern gesetzt

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:16/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:16/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:16/r1.claim: People generally choose the temporary pleasures of worldly life over the hereafter, though the hereafter is better and everlasting; this warns unbelievers and counsels believers to avoid the same error (7:169; 12:109; 93:4).
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:16/r1.anchor: insanların genellikle geçici dünya hayatı ve zevklerini âhirete tercih ettikleri hatırlatılmaktadır

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p369/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p369/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p369/r2.claim: For ويؤثرون, both yāʾ and tāʾ readings and both clear and assimilated articulation are acknowledged; their arguments were given earlier.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p369/r2.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ ويؤثرون ﴾ يقرأ بالياء والتاء وبالاظهار والادغام

IBNMUJAHID:v1p680/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p680/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p680/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr alone reads بل يؤثرون in third person; all other readers address the audience with بل تؤثرون.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p680/r2.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وحده / بل يؤثرون / بالياء وقرأ الباقون ﴿ بل تؤثرون ﴾ بالتاء

QIRAAT-ER:87:16:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:87:16:2#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:87:16:2#1/r1.claim: The verb shifts from second-person plural you prefer to third-person plural they prefer, changing the addressee alignment.
QIRAAT-ER:87:16:2#1/r1.anchor: shifts the imperfect verb from second-person plural ""you prefer"" to third-person plural

ALUSI-FULL:v30p110/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p110/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p110/r1.claim: One account takes bal as a shift from the implied failure to follow the path to success: instead, people prefer worldly life.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p110/r1.anchor: إضراب عن مقدر ينساق إليه الكلام كأنه قيل أثر بيان ما يؤدي إلى الفلاح لا نفعلون ذلك بل تؤثرون

ALUSI-FULL:v30p110/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p110/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p110/r2.claim: Another account takes the shift from describing the heedful and heedless to explaining why reminders do not benefit the rebellious: they choose worldly life.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p110/r2.anchor: وقيل إضراب عن بيان حال المتذكر والمتجنب إلى بيان أنه لا ينفع هذا البيان وأضعافه المتمردين

ALUSI-FULL:v30p110/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p110/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p110/r3.claim: On the first reading, the address may be Meccan disbelievers, whose preference means contentment with this world and complete turning away from the Hereafter.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p110/r3.anchor: على هذا للكفرة الأشقين من أهل مكة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p110/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p110/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p110/r4.claim: Alternatively, the address generalizes to people: preference includes the common tendency to favor worldly pursuits and arrange one's means around them, a meaning attributed to Ibn Masʿūd.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p110/r4.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون لجميع الناس على سبيل التغليب فالمراد بإيثارها ما هو أعم مما ذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p110/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p110/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p110/r5.claim: The shift in address heightens rebuke for disbelievers and, under the general reading, admonition for Muslims as well; some deny any shift by supplying “say.”
ALUSI-FULL:v30p110/r5.anchor: والألتفات على الأول لتشديد التوبيخ وعلى الثاني كذلك في حق الكفرة ولتشديد العتاب في حق المسلمين

ALUSI-FULL:v30p110/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p110/r6.speaker: عبد الله وأبو رجاء والحسن والجحدري وأبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة وأبو عمرو والزعفراني وابن مقسم
ALUSI-FULL:v30p110/r6.claim: These readers recite the verb in the third person, “they prefer,” rather than second-person “you prefer.”
ALUSI-FULL:v30p110/r6.anchor: وقرأعبد الله وأبو رجاء والحسن والجحدري

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p403/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p403/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو ويعقوب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p403/r1.claim: Abu Amr and Yaʿqub read ‘they prefer’ in the third person, referring to the wretched people mentioned; other readers address the audience directly.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p403/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p403/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p403/r2.claim: Ubayy’s reading says ‘rather, you prefer the worldly life,’ supporting the direct-address reading; al-ashqa is singular in form but generic and plural in reference.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p403/r2.anchor: دليله: قراءة أبي بن كعب "بل أنتم تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا"

BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r5.claim: People prefer worldly life and so neglect what would make them happy in the afterlife; the address may target the wretched, be commanded through قل, or address everyone because worldly striving generally predominates.
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r5.anchor: والخطاب للأشقين على الالتفات أو على إضمار قل، أو للكل

BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:13-18/r6.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads the verb in the third person plural rather than second person.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r1.claim: People prefer the low, transient present world because its immediacy captivates sense-bound creatures and consumes time meant for remembrance and purification.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r1.anchor: أي الدنية بالفناء الحاضرة , مع أنها شر وفانية

BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r2.claim: Worldly attachment produces bodily appetites and love of wealth that lead to evil deeds.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r2.anchor: في داء القبقب وهو البطن , والدبدب وهو الفرج , وحب المال

BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p401/r4.claim: The rhetorical pairing leaves rejecting the afterlife implicit after mention of worldly preference, then uses the afterlife's goodness and permanence to imply the world's opposite; it deters from the base and attracts to the lasting.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p404#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p404#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p404#2/r1.claim: The sura follows the warning against worldly preference with a warning against turning from purification through any route other than the prophets' method.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p404#2/r1.anchor: رهب أول هذه من الإعراض عن ذلك مرة , ومن التزكي بغير منهاج الرسل

DURR-FULL:v8p487/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd recited an expanded wording that explicitly contrasts worldly life with the afterlife.
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r2.anchor: عن أبن مسعود رضي الله عنه أنه كان يقرأ / بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة

DURR-FULL:v8p487/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r3.speaker: عرفجة الثقفي
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd stopped at the verse, confessed that they favored worldly life, and explained that its visible pleasures displaced the unseen afterlife; he also read the verb with yāʾ.
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r3.anchor: عن عرفجة الثقفي قال: استقرأت ابن مسعود {سبح اسم ربك الأعلى} فلما بلغ {بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا}

DURR-FULL:v8p487/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r4.claim: At the end of the same report Ibn Masʿūd gives a variant reading with third-person yāʾ: “they prefer.”

DURR-FULL:v8p487/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r5.claim: Qatāda says people choose immediate life except those God protects; the afterlife surpasses this life in goodness and permanence.
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r5.anchor: عن قتادة {خزي في الحياة الدنيا} قال: اختار الناس العاجلة إلا من عصم الله {والآخرة خير}

DURR-FULL:v8p487/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r6.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r6.claim: ʿIkrima says the warning addresses this community and predicts that they will prefer worldly life.
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r6.anchor: عن عكرمة {بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا} قال: يعني هذه الأمة وإنكم ستؤثرون الحياة الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v8p487/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r7.claim: A report from Anas says the testimony of faith protects from divine anger so long as people do not trade their religion for worldly gain; then it is rejected as false.
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r7.anchor: قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: لا إله إلا الله تمنع العباد من سخط الله ما لم يؤثروا صفقة دنياهم

DURR-FULL:v8p487/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r8.claim: A report from Ibn ʿUmar says the testimony leads to Paradise unless mixed with love, preference, accumulation, and contentment with worldly life and tyrants’ deeds.
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r8.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: لا يلقى الله أحد بشهادة أن لا إله إلا الله

DURR-FULL:v8p487/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r9.claim: Abū Mūsā reports the Prophet’s counsel that love for either world harms the other, so one should choose what lasts over what perishes.
DURR-FULL:v8p487/r9.anchor: عن أبي موسى الأشعري رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: من أحب دنياه أضر بآخرته

DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r1.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports the Prophet describing worldly life as the home and wealth of those lacking real home and wealth, gathered by the mindless.
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r1.anchor: دار من لا دار له ومال من لا مال له

DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r2.claim: Mūsā ibn Yasār reports that God created nothing more hated to Him than the world and has never looked at it.
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r2.anchor: عن موسى بن يسار رضي الله عنه أنه بلغه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: إن الله جل ثناؤه لم يخلق خلقا أبغض إليه

DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan attributes to the Prophet the saying that love of worldly life is the root of every sin.
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r3.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: حب الدنيا رأس كل خطيئة

DURR-FULL:v8p488/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r6.claim: Asked whether the Prophet received anything from those scrolls, he recited the passage from purification and prayer through the superiority of the afterlife and the scrolls.
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r6.anchor: هل أنزل عليك شيء مما كان في صحف إبراهيم وموسى قال: يا أبا ذر نعم {قد أفلح من تزكى

ABUHAYYAN:87:16/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:16/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN:87:16/r1.claim: The majority read the verb in the second person, addressing the unbelievers.
ABUHAYYAN:87:16/r1.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { بل تؤثرون } بتاء الخطاب للكفار

ABUHAYYAN:87:16/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:16/r2.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:87:16/r2.claim: Another view addresses both righteous and wicked: the righteous prefer worldly life to gain reward, while the wicked prefer it from desire.
ABUHAYYAN:87:16/r2.anchor: وقيل : خطاب للبر والفاجر ؛ يؤثرها البر

ABUHAYYAN:87:16/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:16/r3.speaker: عبد الله وأبو رجاء والحسن والجحدري وأبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة وأبو عمرو والزعفراني وابن مقسم
ABUHAYYAN:87:16/r3.claim: These readers, including ʿAbd Allāh, Abū Rajāʾ, al-Ḥasan, and Abū ʿAmr, read the verb in the third person with yāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN:87:16/r3.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله وأبو رجاء والحسن والجحدري

ALUSI:87:16/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:16/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:16/r1.claim: Bal shifts from an implied conclusion after the account of what leads to success: you do not pursue it, but prefer worldly life; this may be what is meant by saying it shifts from 87:14.
ALUSI:87:16/r1.anchor: إضراب عن مقدر ينساق إليه الكلام كأنه قيل إثر بيان ما يؤدي إلى الفلاح

ALUSI:87:16/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:16/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:87:16/r2.claim: An alternative says the verse shifts from describing those who remember and avoid the reminder to explaining why admonition does not benefit rebels: they prefer worldly life.
ALUSI:87:16/r2.anchor: وقيل إضراب عن بيان حال المتذكر والمتجنب إلى بيان أنه لا ينفع هذا البيان

ALUSI:87:16/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:16/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:16/r3.claim: If addressed to Meccan unbelievers, preferring worldly life means being content with and settled in it while turning entirely away from the Hereafter, as in 10:7.
ALUSI:87:16/r3.anchor: فالمراد بإيثار الحياة الدنيا هو الرضاء والاطمئنان بها والإعراض عن الآخرة

ALUSI:87:16/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:16/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:16/r4.claim: Alternatively, the address may include all people: preference covers the common tendency to prioritize worldly life in effort and planning; Ibn Masʿūd is cited in support.
ALUSI:87:16/r4.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون لجميع الناس على سبيل التغليب فالمراد بإيثارها ما هو أعم

ALUSI:87:16/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:16/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:16/r5.claim: The shift in address heightens rebuke of unbelievers on the first reading, and rebuke of unbelievers plus reproach of Muslims on the general reading; one view posits an implicit say and no shift.
ALUSI:87:16/r5.anchor: والالتفات على الأول لتشديد التوبيخ وعلى الثاني كذلك في حق الكفرة

ALUSI:87:16/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:16/r6.speaker: عبد الله وأبو رجاء والحسن والجحدري وأبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة وأبو عمرو والزعفراني وابن مقسم
ALUSI:87:16/r6.claim: These readers recite yuʾthirūna with third-person yāʾ instead of second person.
ALUSI:87:16/r6.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله وأبو رجاء والحسن والجحدري وأبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة وأبو عمرو

BAGHAWI:87:16/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:16/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو ويعقوب
BAGHAWI:87:16/r1.claim: Abu ʿAmr and Yaʿqub read the verb in the third person, referring to the most wretched people just mentioned.
BAGHAWI:87:16/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو ، ويعقوب : يؤثرون بالياء ، يعني : الأشقين الذين ذكروا

BAGHAWI:87:16/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:16/r2.speaker: الآخرون
BAGHAWI:87:16/r2.claim: The other readers use the second person; Ubayy ibn Kaʿb's reading, “rather, you prefer,” supports it.
BAGHAWI:87:16/r2.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون بالتاء ، دليله : قراءة أبي بن كعب { بل أنتم تؤثرون }

BAYDAWI:87:16/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:16/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:87:16/r1.claim: You prefer worldly life and therefore fail to do what would bring happiness in the Hereafter.
BAYDAWI:87:16/r1.anchor: بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا فلا تفعلون ما يسعدكم في الآخرة

BAYDAWI:87:16/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:16/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:87:16/r2.claim: The address may shift to the wicked, may have an omitted “say,” or may address everyone because worldly striving is generally more common.
BAYDAWI:87:16/r2.anchor: والخطاب للأشقين على الالتفات أو على إضمار قل أو للكل فإن السعي للدنيا أكثر في الجملة

BAYDAWI:87:16/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:16/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو
BAYDAWI:87:16/r3.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads the verb in the third person plural.

BIQAI:87:16/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:16/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:16/r1.claim: The majority reading addresses the audience directly, a shift signaling extreme anger; Abū ʿAmr retains third person, matching the prior context and its alternate inference.
BIQAI:87:16/r1.anchor: وبالغيب على الأصل عند أبي عمرو

BIQAI:87:16/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:16/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:16/r2.claim: Tuʾthirūn means choosing and privileging; worldly life is low, present, and perishable, yet people single it out for its immediacy.

BIQAI:87:16/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:16/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:16/r3.claim: Sensory attachment occupies people's time like animals bound to what they perceive, keeping them from God's remembrance and self-purification and leaving them to appetite, sex, and wealth.

BIQAI:87:16/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:16/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:16/r4.claim: Biqāʿī casts this blame as the fourth treatment, purging vices by condemning what should be discarded and urging what should be acquired.
BIQAI:87:16/r4.anchor: بالذم على ما ينبغي البراءة منه والحث

DURR:87:16/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:16/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR:87:16/r1.claim: Ibn Masud is reported to read the clause with the addition “over the hereafter.”
DURR:87:16/r1.anchor: أخرج عبد بن حميد عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه أنه كان يقرأ { بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا } على الآخرة .

DURR:87:16/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:16/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR:87:16/r2.claim: In ʿUrfajah al-Thaqafi’s account, Ibn Masud pauses and admits that they chose the immediate world because its adornments, women, food, and drink were visible while the hereafter was veiled from them.
DURR:87:16/r2.anchor: عن عرفجة الثقفي قال : استقرأت ابن مسعود { سبح اسم ربك الأعلى }

DURR:87:16/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:16/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR:87:16/r3.claim: In the same account, Ibn Masud is said to recite the verb in the third person plural, “they prefer.”
DURR:87:16/r3.anchor: عن عرفجة الثقفي قال : استقرأت ابن مسعود { سبح اسم ربك الأعلى }

DURR:87:16/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:16/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR:87:16/r4.claim: Qatada says people choose the present life except those God protects; the hereafter excels in goodness and lasts longer.
DURR:87:16/r4.anchor: عن قتادة { بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا } قال : اختار الناس العاجلة إلا من عصم الله

DURR:87:16/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:16/r5.speaker: عكرمة
DURR:87:16/r5.claim: Ikrimah applies the warning to this community, saying that they will prefer worldly life.
DURR:87:16/r5.anchor: عن عكرمة { بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا } قال : يعني هذه الأمة

DURR:87:16/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī

DURR:87:16/r6.claim: The Prophet says the testimony of God’s oneness protects people from divine anger unless they prefer worldly gain to their religion; then their profession of faith is rejected as false.
DURR:87:16/r6.anchor: عن أنس رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «لا إله إلا الله تمنع العباد من سخط الله

DURR:87:16/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:87:16/r8.claim: The Prophet says loving this world harms one’s hereafter, while loving the hereafter harms one’s worldly life, and urges choosing what endures over what perishes.
DURR:87:16/r8.anchor: عن أبي موسى الأشعري رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : «من أحب دنياه أضر بآخرته

DURR:87:16/r9.claim: The Prophet calls the world the home of one who has no home and the wealth of one who has no wealth, gathered by a person without reason.
DURR:87:16/r9.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «الدنيا دار من لا دار له

DURR:87:16/r11.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «حب الدنيا رأس كل خطيئة

IBNASHUR:87:16/r1.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR:87:16/r1.claim: The majority read the verb with second-person tāʾ, directly addressing the polytheists in the context and shifting from third person.
IBNASHUR:87:16/r1.anchor: قرأ الجمهور { تؤثرون } بمثناة فوقية بصيغة الخطاب

IBNASHUR:87:16/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:16/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNASHUR:87:16/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr alone reads with third-person yāʾ, referring back to the most wretched person entering the Fire.
IBNASHUR:87:16/r2.anchor: وقرأه أبو عمرو وحده بالمثناة التحتية على طريقة الغيبة عائدا إلى

IBNASHUR:87:16/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:16/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:16/r3.claim: Bal has the general sense of turning to what follows; with single words it cancels the previous item or qualifies it.
IBNASHUR:87:16/r3.anchor: معناه الجامع هو الإضراب ، أي انصراف القول أو الحكم

IBNASHUR:87:16/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:16/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:16/r4.claim: Between sentences, bal joins one utterance to another without necessarily sharing or reversing its judgment; it can either cancel the prior meaning or simply shift topics.
IBNASHUR:87:16/r4.anchor: وإذا عطف الجمل فعطفه عطف كلام على كلام وهو عطف لفظي مجرد عن التشريك في الحكم

IBNASHUR:87:16/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:16/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:16/r5.claim: The cancelling use is illustrated by the denial of the claim that the Prophet is possessed, followed by “rather, he brought them the truth.”
IBNASHUR:87:16/r5.anchor: نحو قوله تعالى :  { أم يقولون به جنة بل جاءهم بالحق }

IBNASHUR:87:16/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:16/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:16/r6.claim: The non-cancelling use merely moves from one report to another, as when the text shifts from a just record to hearts being heedless.
IBNASHUR:87:16/r6.anchor: نحو قوله تعالى :  { ولدينا كتاب ينطق بالحق وهم لا يظلمون بل قلوبهم في غمرة من هذا }

IBNASHUR:87:16/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:16/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:16/r7.claim: Here bal may simply move from those who benefit from or avoid the reminder to the reason the wretched avoid it: they prefer worldly life; this is especially clear on Abū ʿAmr’s reading.
IBNASHUR:87:16/r7.anchor: و { بل } هنا عاطفة جملة عطفاً صُورياً

IBNASHUR:87:16/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:16/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:16/r8.claim: On the majority reading, bal shifts from narrating the two groups to rebuking the wretched directly, using an address shift to renew the listener’s attention.
IBNASHUR:87:16/r8.anchor: وأما على قراءة الجمهور فهو إضراب عن حكاية أحوال الفريقين بالانتقال إلى توبيخ أحد الفريقين

IBNASHUR:87:16/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:16/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:16/r9.claim: Alternatively, bal cancels the implication in “successful is whoever purifies” that the wretched might pursue success and join the God-fearing.
IBNASHUR:87:16/r9.anchor: لما تضمنه قوله :  { قد أفلح من تزكى }

IBNASHUR:87:16/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:16/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:16/r10.claim: Īthār is choosing one thing from among several; here it means giving worldly life one’s attention and concern.

IBNASHUR:87:16/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:16/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:16/r11.claim: The comparison is left unstated because the world implies the alternative: polytheists ignore any life beyond the present and dismiss reminders of the hereafter.
IBNASHUR:87:16/r11.anchor: ولم يذكر المؤثر عليه لأن الحياة الدنيا تدل عليه

IBNASHUR:87:16/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:16/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:16/r12.claim: This preference is the object of rebuke because the polytheists disbelieve in the hereafter and refuse to listen when it is described to them.
IBNASHUR:87:16/r12.anchor: فالمشركون لا يؤمنون بالآخرة وإذا ذكروا بالحياة الآخرة وأخبروا بها لم يعيروا سمعهم ذلك

IBNASHUR:87:16/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:16/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:16/r13.claim: Believers also receive this warning: its force matches how much someone neglects salvation for worldly gain that brings afterlife consequences under the law.
IBNASHUR:87:16/r13.anchor: للمؤمنين حظا من هذه الموعظة على طول الدهر

IBNASHUR:87:16/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:16/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:16/r14.claim: Pursuing abundant worldly benefits is not blameworthy if one does not neglect the means of salvation in the hereafter.
IBNASHUR:87:16/r14.anchor: فأما الاستكثار من منافع الدنيا مع عدم إهمال أسباب النجاة في الآخرة فذلك ميدان للهمم

IBNATIYYA:87:16/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:16/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:87:16/r1.claim: Disbelievers prefer worldly life because they deny an afterlife; believers prefer it through sin and overpowering desire, except those God protects.
IBNATIYYA:87:16/r1.anchor: فالكفار يؤثرها إيثار كفر يرى أن لا آخرة ، والمؤمن يؤثرها إيثار معصية وغلبة نفس إلا من عصم الله

IBNATIYYA:87:16/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:16/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA:87:16/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr alone among the Seven reads the verb in third-person plural, referring to the most wretched; Ibn Masʿūd, al-Ḥasan, Abū Rajāʾ, and al-Jaḥdarī also read it so.
IBNATIYYA:87:16/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وحده{[11757]} «يؤثرون » بالياء ، وقال : يعني الأشقين ، وهي قراءة ابن مسعود والحسن وأبي رجاء والجحدري

IBNATIYYA:87:16/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:16/r3.speaker: الباقون
IBNATIYYA:87:16/r3.claim: The other readers use the second-person plural, and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb's codex has the expanded wording, addressing the listeners explicitly.
IBNATIYYA:87:16/r3.anchor: وقرأ الباقون والناس : «تؤثرون » بالتاء على المخاطبة ، وفي حرف أبي بن كعب «بل أنتم تؤثرون »

IBNKATHIR:87:16/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:16/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:87:16/r1.claim: People put worldly life ahead of the afterlife and favor it over what benefits and rectifies their present life and final return.
IBNKATHIR:87:16/r1.anchor: تقدمونها على أمر الآخرة ، وتبدونها على ما فيه نفعهم وصلاحهم في معاشهم ومعادهم

IBNKATHIR:87:17/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:17/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR:87:17/r3.claim: When reciting the verse, Ibn Masud told his companions that they had preferred the world because its adornments, women, food, and drink were visible, while the afterlife was kept from them, so they chose the immediate over the deferred; the report comes through Arfaja al-Thaqafi.
IBNKATHIR:87:17/r3.anchor: ابن مسعود : { سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الأَعْلَى } فلما بلغ : { بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا } ترك القراءة ، وأقبل على أصحابه وقال

IBNKATHIR:87:17/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:17/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:87:17/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir says Ibn Masud’s statement may be an expression of humility and self-reproach, or a description of humankind as a general kind.
IBNKATHIR:87:17/r4.anchor: وهذا منه على وجه التواضع والهضم ، أو هو إخبار عن الجنس من حيث{[29984]}  هو

MAWARDI:87:16/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:16/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI:87:16/r1.claim: If the address concerns disbelievers, it means they prefer worldly life to the Hereafter.
MAWARDI:87:16/r1.anchor: أحدهما : أن المراد بها الكفار ، فيكون تأويلها : بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة

MAWARDI:87:16/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:16/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI:87:16/r2.claim: If it concerns Muslims, it means they prefer accumulating worldly goods in order to increase their reward.
MAWARDI:87:16/r2.anchor: الثاني : أن المراد بها المسلمون ، فيكون تأويلها : يؤثرون الاستكثار من الدنيا للاستكثار من الثواب

NASAFI:87:16/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:16/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:87:16/r1.claim: People prefer worldly life to the afterlife and fail to do what brings salvation.
NASAFI:87:16/r1.anchor: على الآخرة فلا تفعلون ما به تفلحون

NASAFI:87:16/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:16/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASAFI:87:16/r2.claim: Abu Amr reads the verb in the third-person plural, “they prefer,” identifying the addressees as unbelievers.
NASAFI:87:16/r2.anchor: والمخاطب به الكافرون دليله قراءة أبي عمرو { يؤثرون } بالياء

QURTUBI:87:16/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:16/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:16/r1.claim: The majority read in the second person, tuthirūn; Ubay's reading adds antum and confirms that address.
QURTUBI:87:16/r1.anchor: قراءة العامة " بل تؤثرون " بالتاء ، تصديقه قراءة أُبيّ " بل أنتم تؤثرون "

QURTUBI:87:16/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:16/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو ونصر بن عاصم
QURTUBI:87:16/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim read yuʾthirūn in the third person, with the most wretched understood as the subject.
QURTUBI:87:16/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو ونصر بن عاصم " بل يؤثرون " بالياء على الغيبة

QURTUBI:87:16/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:16/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:16/r3.claim: On the second-person reading, the address is to Muslims who prefer accumulating worldly life in order to accumulate reward.
QURTUBI:87:16/r3.anchor: وعلى الأول فيكون تأويلها بل تؤثرون أيها المسلمون الاستكثار من الدنيا ، للاستكثار من الثواب

QURTUBI:87:16/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:16/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI:87:16/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿūd explains that people choose the present world's ready food, drink, pleasures, and beauty, while the afterlife is unseen; they take the immediate and leave the deferred.
QURTUBI:87:16/r4.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود أنه قرأ هذه الآية ، فقال : أتدرون لم آثرنا الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة ؟

QURTUBI:87:16/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:16/r5.speaker: أبو موسى
QURTUBI:87:16/r5.claim: Anas reports that Abū Mūsā urged him to remember God when travelers dwelt on worldly matters; Abū Mūsā said the world hastens while the afterlife is hidden, and seeing it would leave no one wavering or preferring this life.
QURTUBI:87:16/r5.anchor: وروى ثابت عن أنس قال : كنا مع أبي موسى في مسير ، والناس يتكلمون ويذكرون الدنيا

RAZI:87:16/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:16/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:87:16/r1.claim: The common reading addresses the audience in the second person, supported by Ubayy’s written form.
RAZI:87:16/r1.anchor: قراءة العامة بالتاء ويؤكده حرف أبي

RAZI:87:16/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:16/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:87:16/r2.claim: The second-person reading means that people prefer worldly deeds to deeds for the afterlife.
RAZI:87:16/r2.anchor: أي بل أنتم تؤثرون عمل الدنيا على عمل الآخرة

RAZI:87:16/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:16/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
RAZI:87:16/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says worldly food, drink, women, pleasures, and beauty are present and hastened, while the afterlife is unseen and deferred, so people choose the immediate.
RAZI:87:16/r3.anchor: إن الدنيا أحضرت ، وعجل لنا طعامها وشرابها

RAZI:87:16/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:16/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
RAZI:87:16/r4.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads the verb in the third person, meaning that the most wretched prefer worldly life.
RAZI:87:16/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو : ( يؤثرون ) بالياء يعني الأشقى

TAB:87:16/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:16/r1.speaker: author
TAB:87:16/r1.claim: People favor worldly adornment over the Hereafter, although the Hereafter is better in goodness and more lasting because this life ends while the next endures.
TAB:87:16/r1.anchor: بل تؤثرون أيها الناس زينة الحياة الدنيا

TAB:87:16/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:16/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB:87:16/r2.claim: Qatada says people choose the immediate life except those God preserves; the Hereafter surpasses it in goodness and permanence.
TAB:87:16/r2.anchor: عن قتادة بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ الْحَياةَ الدّنيْا فاختار الناس العاجلة

TAB:87:16/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:16/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB:87:16/r3.claim: While reciting the sūra, Ibn Masʿūd said people chose worldly life because they could see its pleasures, while the Hereafter was hidden from them.
TAB:87:16/r3.anchor: استقرأت ابن مسعود سَبّحِ اسْمَ رَبّكَ الأعْلَى

TAB:87:16/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:16/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
TAB:87:16/r4.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads the verb in the third person with yāʾ, taking the subject to be the wretched.
TAB:87:16/r4.anchor: إلا أبا عمرو ،   فإنه قرأه بالياء

TAB:87:16/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:16/r5.speaker: author
TAB:87:16/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the second-person tāʾ reading because the authoritative readers agree on it.
TAB:87:16/r5.anchor: والذي لا أوثر عليه في قراءة ذلك التاء

TAB:87:16/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:16/r6.speaker: أبيّ
TAB:87:16/r6.claim: Ubayy's reading adds antum, ‘you’, which also supports the second-person reading.
TAB:87:16/r6.anchor: وذُكر أن ذلك في قراءة أُبيّ :  بَلْ أنْتُمْ تُؤْثِرُونَ

SIBAWAYH:هذابابالإدغامفيالحروفالمتقاربةا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:هذابابالإدغامفيالحروفالمتقاربةا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:هذابابالإدغامفيالحروفالمتقاربةا.claim: A reading assimilates the lām of bal into tāʾ in bal tuʾthirūna al-ḥayāta al-dunyā, yielding batūthirūna.
SIBAWAYH:هذابابالإدغامفيالحروفالمتقاربةا.anchor: وقد قرئ بها ^ ( بتؤثرون الحياة الدنيا ) ^ فأدغم اللام في التاء

BURHAN:v4p259/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p259/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p259/r1.claim: At times بل leaves one line of discourse and begins a second; the cited passages repeatedly break from a prior statement to a fresh assertion.
BURHAN:v4p259/r1.anchor: ومنه أيضا ﴿ قد أفلح من تزكى وذكر اسم ربه فصلى بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا

BURHAN:v4p259/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p259/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p259/r2.claim: When بل precedes a single word after an affirmative, it retracts the first assertion and affirms what follows; the same pattern can follow a verb phrase.
BURHAN:v4p259/r2.anchor: فقال النحاة هي تجعل ما قبلها كالمسكوت عنه

BURHAN:v4p259/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p259/r3.speaker: المبرد
BURHAN:v4p259/r3.claim: Al-Mubarrad agrees on the basic distinction but also allows بل after a negative or prohibition to transfer the construction to what follows.
BURHAN:v4p259/r3.anchor: ووافق المبرد على ما ذكرنا غير أنه أجاز مع ذلك أن تكون ناقلة مع النهى أو النفى

NASHR:v2p399#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p399#2/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p399#2/r3.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads بل تؤثرون in third person; Ibn Mihrān uniquely transmits this from Rawḥ, with mixed reports for Ruways, while the others use direct address.
NASHR:v2p399#2/r3.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو بالغيب، وانفرد ابن مهران بذلك عن روح في كل كتبه

QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r23.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r23.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r23.claim: People prefer worldly interests, putting their own shares of worldly life before God's rights.
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r23.anchor: تميلون إليها ؛ فتقدمون حظوظكم منها على حقوق الله تعالى

FARRA:v3p256/r14.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p256/r14.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p256/r14.claim: Reciters agree on the second-person form.

FARRA:v3p256/r15.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p256/r15.speaker: أبي
FARRA:v3p256/r15.claim: Ubayy's reading explicitly adds 'you' to clarify the second-person plural form.
FARRA:v3p256/r15.anchor: وهي في قراءة أبي: «بل أنتم تؤثرون الحياة» تحقيقا لمن قرأ بالتاء

FARRA:v3p256/r16.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p256/r16.speaker: بعض القراء
FARRA:v3p256/r16.claim: Some reciters read the verb in the third-person plural.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r3.claim: Disbelievers prefer transient life to the better, eternal afterlife, so the Prophet's message finds no root in their hearts despite its continuity with earlier prophetic teaching.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r3.anchor: giving preference to this world over the next

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p280/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p280/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p280/r2.claim: The Quraysh's hostility comes from attachment to worldly interests: they invent doubts rather than risk those interests for the Hereafter, sacrificing eternal reward for transient life.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p280/r2.anchor: the Hereafter is more lasting and permanent

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r13.claim: The majority read tuʾthirūna as direct address to the unbelievers; another view addresses both righteous and wicked, who prefer the world for different reasons.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r13.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: بل تؤثرون بتاء الخطاب للكفار. وقيل: خطاب للبر والفاجر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r14.speaker: عبد الله وأبو رجاء والحسن والجحدري وأبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة وأبو عمرو والزعفراني وابن مقسم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r14.claim: These readers pronounce yuʾthirūna in the third person rather than addressing the audience.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p458/r14.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله وأبو رجاء والحسن والجحدري وأبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة وأبو عمرو
